name: Extract intents from prose
description: plan(prose) sends the prose to an LLM through an AskJson transport with a fixed system prompt and JSON Schema (step "extract"). The answer lists intents, each with a statement, a kind (behavior, invariant, preserve, non-functional), a provability (formal, empirical, beyond-proof), a beyondProofReason ("none" or one of the five reasons) and a verbatim quote; decisions that reference intents by zero-based index; and notPromised items. The answer becomes an intent artifact (lastro: intent-artifact/v0) with ids I1, I2... in answer order, every intent in status proposed, decisions D1, D2... with origin extraction, and the team's review policy attached. Without an LLM transport or a custom extractor, plan() throws.

name: Anchor every intent to the prose
description: Each intent stores its quote with start and end offsets into the prose (the intent map). The quote is searched verbatim first, then ignoring case and runs of whitespace from a word boundary. If any quote is not found, or a beyond-proof intent has no reason, or a reason is unknown, or a decision has fewer than two options, a recommended index out of range or an unknown intent, the whole extraction is rejected with an ArtifactError listing every problem.

name: Turn ambiguity into decision cards
description: The extraction prompt tells the model not to guess when the prose is ambiguous and to return a decision instead: one question, two to four options each with a consequence, and the index of the recommended option, preferably about cases the author has not considered. Each becomes a decision card tied to the intents it concerns. A card with origin extraction records the chosen option when answered and creates no intent.

name: Record what is not promised
description: The extraction returns notPromised: things a reader might assume that the prose does not promise. They are stored on the artifact, reviewers can append more, they are part of the frozen hash, they are sent to the deriver, and the receipt lists them under Not promised.

name: Review intents
description: review(artifact, reviewer) returns a chainable review on a copy of the artifact (a frozen artifact is thawed first). approve(ids) marks intents approved (an amended intent stays amended) and adds the reviewer to approvals once; approveAll() approves every intent that is not rejected; reject(id, note) sets status rejected, records the note with the reviewer's name and clears approvals; amend(id, statement, patch?, note?) keeps the first original statement, rewrites the statement (optionally kind, provability or beyond-proof reason), sets status amended and resets approvals to the amender alone. done() returns the new artifact; unknown ids throw.

name: Add an intent the extractor missed
description: During review, add(draft) appends an intent with the next id, status approved and a note saying it was added by a reviewer. Its quote is anchored when found in the prose; otherwise the note says it is not in the prose. Reviewers can also append notPromised items.

name: Enforce the team's approval policy
description: createLastro({ requiredApprovals }) sets how many distinct reviewers must approve each intent (default 1, and never less than 1). An approved or amended intent counts its distinct approvers, or one when it has no approver list; proposed and rejected intents count zero. pending() lists every proposed intent with no approval as not reviewed, every non-rejected intent below the policy with how many approvals it still needs, and every unanswered decision. Only intents that reach the policy are approved intents, the only ones sent to derivation; rejected intents never block.

name: Answer decision cards
description: answer(decisionId, option) records the chosen option; an unknown decision or an option out of range throws. For an extraction decision that is all. For a decision raised later (a contradiction), the answer also creates, or rewrites, an intent linked to the decision whose statement is the question plus the chosen option and its consequence; that intent starts proposed with no approvals and must be reviewed like any other.

name: Freeze the reviewed intents
description: freeze() refuses with every pending item while anything is pending. Otherwise it returns a copy with hash = sha256 over canonical JSON (keys sorted, undefined dropped) of the artifact without its hash. A frozen artifact cannot be reviewed; thaw() returns an unfrozen copy. isIntact() recomputes the hash, so any edit after the freeze is detected, and plan validation rejects an artifact that is not frozen or not intact.

name: Keep the review when the prose changes
description: plan(prose, previous) extracts again and carries the previous review over. A new intent whose statement equals, ignoring case and whitespace, the statement of a previously reviewed (non-proposed) intent takes its status, approvals, review note and original statement. If instead the AI repeats the original reading of an amended intent for the same quote, the amendment is reapplied with its approvals. Everything else stays proposed. Decisions with the same question keep their answer when the option still exists, and the previous policy is kept. Decisions raised by the consistency check, and their intents, are not carried.

name: Declare the proof vocabulary
description: A model has a name, inputs and outputs, each a domain: bool, enum of strings or numbers, int with optional min and max, or string with optional examples; plus named defs (parameters and an LSL body). Bool, enum and bounded int domains are finite and enumerable in a fixed, sorted-key order; unbounded ints and strings are not. Facts supplied by trusted external pieces enter as inputs. A model with no outputs is rejected by plan validation.

name: Write specs in LSL
description: LSL expressions are JSON: const, var (in.<input> or out.<output>, or a def parameter), call of a def, or op with args among and, or, not, implies, iff, eq, neq, lt, le, gt, ge, add, sub, mul, ite and in, each with a fixed arity. They are interpreted, never eval'ed, with strict typing (a non-boolean where a boolean is expected, or a non-number in arithmetic, is an error), unbound variables rejected, and recursion capped at depth 64. validateExpr checks shape, arity and variables against the model; show prints readable notation; toSmtLib compiles requires => ensures to an SMT-LIB2 script that asserts its negation.

name: Derive the proof plan
description: spec(artifact) freezes the artifact and asks the LLM (step "derive") with the model, the approved intents only, each decision's question and answer (the chosen or else the recommended option) and notPromised. The answer has clauses (id, intents, description, requires and ensures as LSL JSON strings, assumptions used), assumptions, scenarios (concrete input as a JSON string and an LSL expect) and beyondProof items. Every expression is parsed and validated; the result is a proof plan (proof-plan/v0) bound to the artifact hash. Without an LLM transport or a custom deriver, spec() throws.

name: Validate the proof plan
description: Before anything is verified, the plan is checked: the artifact is frozen and intact and the plan was derived from its hash; the model has outputs and valid defs; ids are unique; every clause, assumption, scenario and beyond-proof item references at least one known and approved intent (never a rejected one); expressions use only the model; clauses cite known assumptions; assumptions cite known scenarios; each scenario gives an in-domain value for every input; beyond-proof reasons are known. Any error throws a PlanError with all problems. Approved intents covered by nothing are not errors: they are reported as gaps.

name: Return contradictions to the team
description: After derivation, a consistency check enumerates every output (when there are at most 4096) for each input and looks for inputs where no output satisfies all applicable clauses. Each distinct set of conflicting clauses becomes a decision card (origin consistency-check) asking which clause should give way, with one option per clause and the first recommended. spec.ok is false when any exist. returnDecisions(spec) thaws the artifact and appends these cards, skipping questions it already has, so the artifact cannot be frozen until they are answered and the intents their answers create are approved. The Rust prover runs the same check.

name: Prove a clause over a finite domain
description: prove(spec, subject) runs the code on every input of the model when the input space has at most 100,000 points. Outputs outside their domain and inputs where the code throws are recorded as invalid runs and noted on every clause. A clause whose if-part applies to at least one run and whose then-part holds on every applicable run is proved, with formal evidence and the number of inputs checked.

name: Give evidence over large domains
description: When the input space exceeds 100,000 points or is unbounded, the code runs on 2,000 samples drawn with a fixed seed (42) by a deterministic generator, biased toward int bounds and zero and toward declared string examples. A clause that holds on every applicable sample is evidenced, never proved, with empirical evidence and a failure-rate upper bound at 95% confidence of 3/N (rule of three) over the N applicable samples.

name: Report counterexamples
description: The first applicable run that breaks a clause makes it violated and is kept as its counterexample (input and output); the evidence is formal when the run was exhaustive and empirical when sampled. An error while evaluating a clause also makes it violated, with the error noted.

name: Catch clauses that prove nothing
description: A clause whose if-part no run satisfies is vacuous. A clause that held is then tested against planted output mutants (negate each bool output, force each output with at most 16 values to each value, shift each int output by +1 and -1): if it rejects none, it is weak. Both are listed as spec gaps for the team, not code failures. The TypeScript engine keeps the formal or empirical evidence label on a weak clause while the Rust prover labels it none; verdicts are what the cross-check compares.

name: Check recorded production runs
description: prove(spec, subject, { traces }) also checks recorded real input/output pairs. A trace that breaks a clause makes it violated with empirical evidence and the violating trace (and its reference) in the result; if the clause was proved on the model, the note says a trusted piece does not hold. With traces but no subject, a clause that holds on every applicable trace is evidenced, with the rule-of-three bound.

name: Run Given/When/Then scenarios
description: Each scenario runs the code on its concrete input and checks its LSL expectation over input and output. It passes or fails, with the output or the error; with no subject every scenario fails. Scenarios are empirical evidence, and assumptions list the scenarios that check them.

name: Track trusted pieces
description: Each assumption names a trusted piece (external code or a world fact), its contract, what you accept, what breaks if it is wrong and the scenarios that check it. Clauses list the assumptions they rely on. An intent backed by assumptions gets trusted evidence and, when all its clauses are proved, the verdict proved-under-assumptions. The receipt shows each piece with its scenarios passed, failed or planned.

name: Mark where proof stops
description: Beyond-proof items tie an intent to one of five reasons (external-code, world-facts, termination-timing, human-judgment, unstated) with a note. An intent with beyond-proof items and no useful clause gets the verdict beyond-proof, with notes and any passing scenarios as partial evidence. The receipt lists them under Where proof stops.

name: Roll up a verdict per intent
description: Each approved intent gets one verdict, in this order: gap if nothing covers it; violated if any of its clauses is violated or scenarios failed; beyond-proof if it has beyond-proof items and no proved or evidenced clause; evidenced with confidence 0 if it has only scenarios or only assumptions; gap if nothing useful remains; proved, or proved-under-assumptions when it relies on assumptions, if every clause is proved (confidence 1); otherwise evidenced with confidence 1 minus the largest failure-rate bound. The report is ok only with no violated intent, no gap and no contradiction.

name: Cross-check with an independent prover
description: With a Rust prover (lastro-core, loaded as WASM in TypeScript or run as the native lastro-prove binary from Go and .NET), prove() tabulates the code over the whole input space and the prover re-checks every clause from that table. The prover drops out-of-domain rows, counts missing inputs and nondeterministic rows, and calls coverage complete only when every input appears once; it says proved only with complete coverage, checks vacuity, mutants and consistency itself, and returns a SHA-256 digest of the table. The proof is ok only if the SDK report is ok, the prover is ok and both engines give every clause the same verdict.

name: Render a receipt
description: The receipt is Markdown for a pull request: the overall result and counts per verdict; the intents and plan hashes; the Rust check with coverage, table digest and whether verdicts agree; a table of intents with verdict, evidence, confidence and what backs each; notes; each clause with verdict, evidence, method (exhaustive, samples with failure bound, traces), mutants killed, formal statement, counterexample, violating trace and notes; scenarios; trusted pieces; where proof stops; not promised; and pending contradictions.

name: Hand failures to whoever writes the code
description: prove() returns failures (each violated clause or failed scenario with its intents, description, formal statement, counterexample input and output) and specGaps (vacuous or weak clauses, intents with no obligation, contradictions). agentFeedback() renders the failures as a brief telling the implementer to make each obligation hold for every input without breaking the others, or says every proof passes and lists the spec gaps. Lastro never writes the implementation.

name: Explain one run
description: explainRun(plan, input, output) reports, for each clause, whether its if-part is false, it holds, it fails, or evaluating it raised an error.

name: Review gaps the proofs cannot see
description: gapReview(spec, source) sends the approved intents, the clauses in readable notation, the trusted pieces, the beyond-proof items and the source code to the LLM (step "gap-review"). It returns gaps tied to intents (partly captured meaning, reliance on an unmodeled input or trusted piece, an intent with no clause), each with a suggestion and a severity. They are evidence for humans, never proof, and an empty list is valid.

name: Run the pipeline from a CLI
description: The CLIs (lastro in TypeScript and .NET, lastro-go in Go) run init --model model.json [--approvals N], plan <prose-file>, status, review --as <name> approve|approve-all|amend|reject|answer, spec, prove and feedback. Each prints one JSON object and keeps state in a workspace directory (default .lastro, --dir to change): config.json, intents.json, spec.json, proof.json and receipt.md. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 not ok (review pending, contradictions, failing proofs), 2 usage or error, 3 an LLM answer is needed. spec refuses while review is pending and, on contradictions, writes the returned decisions back to intents.json.

name: Hand the AI steps to the calling agent
description: With --llm handoff (the default when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set), each AI request gets a deterministic id from the step and a hash of the request. If the answer file llm/<id>.answer.json exists it is used; otherwise the CLI writes llm/<id>.request.json (instructions, system prompt, user data, JSON Schema) and exits 3 naming the answer path. The calling agent writes its JSON answer there and reruns the command. Ids match across the TypeScript, .NET and Go CLIs.

name: Extract from one section of a document
description: In the TypeScript CLI, plan <file> --section <heading> uses only the body of the Markdown section whose heading matches (ignoring case), up to the next heading of the same or a higher level; an unknown heading is an error (exit 2). One versioned document can then feed several workspaces.

name: Run the AI steps on Claude
description: The Claude transport (lastro/claude in TypeScript, Lastro.Claude in .NET, the claude package in Go) calls the Anthropic Messages API with the step's system prompt, JSON-schema structured output, adaptive thinking and high effort by default, and parses the JSON answer. A refusal or a truncated answer raises an error. The CLIs use it when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set or with --llm anthropic.

name: Plug in any LLM transport
description: The AI steps are transport-free: prompts, schemas and deterministic converters behind one AskJson function that takes the step, system prompt, user content and schema and returns JSON. Any transport works (an API, an in-browser model, a test double), and createLastro also accepts a custom extractor or deriver, including static ones. Nothing the LLM returns is trusted: quotes are anchored, LSL is validated and plans are checked.

name: Use Lastro from TypeScript, .NET or Go
description: Three SDKs expose the same pipeline (plan, review, pending, spec, returnDecisions, prove, gap review) with the same data model, wire format, canonical hashes, seeded sampling, verdicts, receipts and prompts. Cross-check tests compare the .NET and Go reports and hashes with the TypeScript SDK, and all three with the Rust prover, on the reference login and its planted bugs.

name: Share one workspace across CLIs
description: The TypeScript, .NET and Go CLIs read and write the same .lastro/ files, so one can plan, another review, and a third derive and prove. An artifact frozen by one SDK is intact for the others and a plan has the same hash in all three.

name: Prove code written in any language
description: The code under proof is a subject: a function from inputs to outputs. The TypeScript CLI imports a JavaScript module export (default or --export name); the .NET CLI loads a public static method from an assembly; the Go SDK takes a Go function, a process that reads one JSON input per line and writes one JSON output per line (prove --cmd), or a recorded input/output table (prove --table), where an input with no row is an error.

name: Explore the pipeline in the sandbox
description: A web app (Vite, React, shadcn/ui) runs the real TypeScript SDK and the WASM prover on a store-login example. The prose panel shows the intent map, intent cards (approve, amend, reject) and decision cards, with reviewers Ana and Bruno and a one- or two-approval policy; edited prose is extracted again by Claude (the page's Claude on claude.ai, or a dev-server endpoint with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), the review is carried over, and a new plan is derived. The code panel edits the implementation, plants bugs shown as a diff and shows the feedback for a coding agent. The contrast panel shows per-clause verdicts from both engines, mutants, runnable counterexamples, LSL and SMT-LIB2, the intent roll-up, trusted pieces, where proof stops, a production-trace toggle, a single-login runner and the receipt.
